query: How will we represent time-varying prophylaxis exposure and interruptions in Cox, recurrent-event, and marginal structural models?

response.query: How will we represent time-varying prophylaxis exposure and interruptions in Cox, recurrent-event, and marginal structural models?
response.answer: Time-varying prophylaxis exposure and interruptions are represented using time-dependent covariates in Cox models, person-time analysis in recurrent-event models, and time-varying exposure variables in marginal structural models.

results.title: 1882-R-MiniCHOP (rituximab CYCLOPHOSPHamide ...
results.content: Any dose modification should be based on clinical judgement, and the individual patient’s situation including but not limited to treatment intent (curative vs palliative), the anti-cancer regimen (single versus combination therapy versus chemotherapy versus immunotherapy), biology of the cancer (site, size, mutations, metastases), other treatment related side effects, additional co-morbidities, performance status and patient preferences. There are concerns about the tolerability and efficacy of chemotherapy in the elderly due to the paucity of data in this patient population and the evidence that dose reductions in the treatment of DLBCL affects overall survival.10, 11 There is also greater variability in drug pharmacokinetics in the elderly for example older women have reduced rituximab clearance, resulting in higher serum levels and prolonged exposure times.12 The addition of rituximab to chemotherapy in the elderly may offset the potential negative effect of chemotherapy dose reduction, leading to acceptable efficacy and reduced toxicity.2, 6, 7, 8. In the rituximab era, several large studies have suggested that full-dose rituximab plus cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone (R-CHOP) might be the best treatment for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) aged 60 years and older.

results.title: 3797-Lenalidomide maintenance post autologous transplant
results.content: CONCLUSIONS: Lenalidomide maintenance therapy, initiated at day 100 after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, was associated with more toxicity and second cancers but a significantly longer time to disease progression and significantly improved overall survival among patients with myeloma.
